Welcome to Colony Flow Level 1 where you take charge of a hungry ant colony. This beginner stage introduces the core mechanics of matching colored blocks to a beautiful pixel art puzzle. You must guide your ants to eat every single food tile without jamming your tray. Learning how to manage your ants right here sets you up for success in all the future puzzles. I play every single level to figure out the best routes so you do not have to guess. Follow my exact moves below and you will clear this board on your very first try.
Colony Flow Level 1 Overview
What You Are Working With
The puzzle board features a large pixel art star sitting right above the ant nest hole at the bottom of the screen. The star has three distinct layers of food tiles that you must clear. The outer border consists entirely of bright orange tiles. Inside the orange border sits a middle layer of yellow tiles. The very center of the star holds a core of white tiles. Below the puzzle board you will find a tray loaded with numbered colored blocks. The top layer of the tray holds a single orange block with the number fourteen. Underneath that top block you see two yellow fifteen blocks and a white four block. The bottom rows contain more white blocks along with a mix of orange and yellow blocks. The game gives you exactly five waiting slots at the very bottom edge. You tap blocks from the tray to place them into these slots. Once a block hits a slot the ants activate and go to work.
Level 1 Objective
Your primary goal is to completely clear the pixel art star picture from the board. You win when the ants eat every single orange yellow and white tile leaving the entire board totally empty. You achieve this by pulling blocks from the tray into the waiting slots in the correct sequence. The puzzle ends in an immediate loss if you fill all five waiting slots with blocks that have no clear path to their matching food tiles. You must always ensure that at least one block in your waiting slots has active ants clearing food.
Colony Flow Level 1 Step by Step Solution
Step 1: Pull the first orange block to clear the bottom right border.
You start the level with only one available block sitting at the very top of the tray stack. Tap this orange fourteen block to drop it into your first available waiting slot. Instantly a steady stream of orange colored ants pours out of the round nest hole and grabs pieces of the block. They carry the food up the right side of the board and begin eating the bottom right edge of the orange star border. The number fourteen on the block counts down rapidly as the ants do their job. This initial move carves away a large chunk of the outer border and frees up the next row of blocks hidden in your tray. You keep your remaining four slots totally empty and safe.
Step 2: Drop the two yellow blocks to start on the middle layer.
With the first orange block completely gone you now have clear access to the yellow blocks in the tray. Pull the two yellow fifteen blocks down into your empty waiting slots. Yellow ants will quickly emerge and march toward the bottom and left sections of the star puzzle. They push past the cleared sections of the outer orange layer to attack the yellow food tiles directly. Letting both yellow blocks run at the exact same time keeps the ants flowing quickly and clears a massive portion of the middle layer. Your waiting slots remain perfectly safe from jamming because the yellow ants have wide open paths to their matching colors on the board.
Step 3: Activate the white block to attack the center core.
Now that the yellow ants have opened up wide paths through the middle layer you can safely bring a white block into play. Tap the white four block from the tray to send it to your waiting slots. White ants spawn immediately and march straight up the middle of the open board. They dive directly into the center of the star to eat the white core tiles. Since you cleared the lower orange and yellow tiles earlier the white ants face no traffic jams at all. They easily reach the center and chew away the white food pieces while the yellow ants continue working around them.
Step 4: Bring in another orange block for the left border.
While the white and yellow ants continue their steady work you should pull the next orange fourteen block into an open slot. The newly spawned orange ants will target the left side of the star border. They wrap around the outer left edge and quickly dismantle the remaining orange tiles on the left wing of the star. Keeping multiple colors active at once ensures you constantly shrink the picture and maintain momentum. You still have plenty of open waiting slots available so the board remains completely safe from a dead end loss condition.
Step 5: Clear the remaining white core pieces with a final white block.
The center of the star still has a few white tiles left to clear. Pull the remaining white four block from the tray to finish off the core completely. The white ants will easily march into the fully opened center and consume the last remaining white food tiles. The entire middle of the star disappears from the board at this exact point. You only have the top sections of the orange and yellow layers left on the screen. The puzzle board is now wide open and the ants have massive paths to walk along without bumping into each other.
Step 6: Deploy a yellow block to clean up the upper middle section.
Next you need to clear out the top yellow portion of the star. Tap the next yellow block in your tray and watch it drop into a waiting slot. The yellow ants stream out of the hole and head straight for the top sections of the puzzle. They eat away all the remaining yellow tiles situated under the top point of the star. The number on your yellow block counts all the way down to zero and the block vanishes from your slot. This successful clear opens up your slots for the final sequence of moves required to win the game.
Step 7: Play the final orange blocks to clear the top point of the star.
You are now completely ready to win the level. Pull the final orange blocks from the bottom row of your tray. The orange ants flood the board one last time and march all the way up to the very top point of the star shape. They surround the last remaining orange tiles and eat them away rapidly. Once the final orange tile disappears the board sits completely empty. The ants return to the nest hole and you successfully complete the level.
Overall Strategy to Clear Level 1 Board
Always clear the blocking outer colors before pulling inner colors into your slots. The orange border of the star physically prevents ants from easily reaching the inner layers at the start of the level. You must deploy the top orange block first to carve a safe path. If you try to force other colors into the waiting slots before their path is ready you risk filling all five slots and instantly losing the game.
Manage your five waiting slots by carefully watching the numbers printed on the blocks. The number tells you exactly how many ants will spawn from that specific block. Larger numbers like the fifteen on the yellow blocks take much longer to clear. You should balance high number blocks with low number blocks like the four on the white blocks so your slots empty at a steady and predictable pace.
Attack one side of the board at a time if the screen gets too crowded. In this specific level the bottom right section opens up first. Letting the ants clear entire chunks of the right side gives subsequent ants plenty of room to walk up the left side of the screen. Spreading the ants out across different zones prevents them from bumping into each other and slowing down the block timer.
Keep a close eye on the tray stack order before making a move. You can only pick blocks that sit fully exposed on top of the pile. Plan your color matching around what the tray gives you next. Since the white blocks stay buried under the orange and yellow blocks at the start you have to focus entirely on the outer and middle layers of the star first by design.
Never leave blocks stranded in your tray. You win the game by clearing the entire picture but you also need to use up the relevant blocks provided in the stack. Pay close attention to the block colors and match them to the remaining food tiles on the screen. If you only have orange tiles left on the top of the star make sure you pull the orange blocks to finish the job. Leaving the wrong colors in your slots prevents you from feeding the right ants and reaching the final victory screen.
Final Thought
Colony Flow Level 1 serves as the absolute perfect introduction to managing your ant paths and tray slots. By peeling away the outer orange border first you create highly efficient natural highways for the yellow and white ants to reach the inner sections of the star. Take your time and never overcrowd your waiting slots with unplayable colors. If you find any single part of this written guide hard to follow you should definitely watch the video above this article to see exactly how the ants clear the board.

Colony Flow Level 2 presents a beautiful pixel art heart that you must clear away. You feed your hungry ant colony by matching colored blocks from the bottom tray to the tiles in the picture. I play every level to test the best moves and find the safest path to victory. The challenge here comes from managing massive numbers on your blocks without plugging up your limited space. Here is my complete guide to solving this puzzle without jamming your waiting slots.
Colony Flow Level 2 Overview
What You Are Working With
The puzzle board features a large heart shape made of three different colors. The top and bottom sections consist of bright pink tiles. The middle section contains light blue tiles. Right in the center of the blue section sits a yellow shape that looks exactly like a bow tie. All these tiles sit directly above a nest hole where your colony lives.
At the bottom of your screen is the tray holding your numbered blocks. The top row has three pink blocks that all start at the number 37. The next row down holds three light blue blocks. Two of these blue blocks are numbered 37 and the middle one is numbered 38. The bottom portion of the tray contains three yellow blocks. These yellow blocks are much smaller and carry the numbers 8, 9, and 8. Between the tray and the board are your five empty waiting slots. You send blocks into these slots to release the ants.
Level 2 Objective
Your goal is to clear the entire heart from the board by feeding every single tile to your ant colony. You win when the picture is completely gone and your ants finish cleaning up the screen. You lose if you fill all five waiting slots with blocks that have no clear path to their matching tiles. Keeping at least one active color moving at all times is your primary objective. This ensures the numbers keep dropping and the slots eventually empty out.
Colony Flow Level 2 Step by Step Solution
Step 1: Pull three pink blocks to attack the bottom point of the heart.
You want to start at the closest point to the nest hole. The bottom tip of the heart is made entirely of pink tiles. Tap the three pink blocks in the top row of your tray to move them up into your waiting slots. All three blocks start at 37. Pink ants will immediately stream out of the nest hole and begin eating the bottom point of the heart. You will see the numbers on your blocks count down quickly from 37 to 30, 33, and 36 as the ants grab their food. Clearing this bottom point is vital. It opens up empty space around the outside edges of the heart. This space creates a clear travel path so the ants can reach the upper sections later in the round.
Step 2: Add two light blue blocks to start clearing the middle section.
Once the pink ants eat away the bottom tip, the light blue tiles become fully exposed to the board. Tap two of the light blue blocks from your tray to move them into your remaining waiting slots. I used the first blue 37 block and the blue 38 block for this move. Your five waiting slots are now completely full. You have three pink blocks and two light blue blocks active at the exact same time. Blue ants will join the pink ants on the board. The blue ants will target the light blue tiles on the lower edges of the middle section. The pink ants will continue traveling up the newly opened sides of the heart to reach the top pink section. The board will be swarming with two distinct colors of ants working in harmony.
Step 3: Wait patiently for a pink block to finish completely.
Your waiting slots are full right now so you cannot pull any more blocks from the tray. Do not panic and do not try to force any strange moves. Simply watch the ants do their work across the board. The pink ants will wrap all the way around the outer edges of the heart to reach the massive pink section at the very top. The blue ants will chew steadily through the light blue tiles in the middle. You will see the numbers on your pink blocks drop into the low single digits like 14 and 9. Eventually one of the pink blocks will hit zero. The block will expand in a quick visual animation and disappear completely from your waiting slots. This crucial moment opens up a free slot for your next move.
Step 4: Pull the final light blue block to clear the rest of the blue tiles.
Now that you have an open space in your waiting queue, you can pull the next color. Tap the final light blue 37 block from your tray. The blue ants will get a fresh burst of numbers to work with and will push deeper into the center of the heart. By this time your remaining pink blocks are also counting down to zero. A second pink block will finish and vanish from the slots. The heart shape will be mostly destroyed at this stage of the game. Only a few scattered pink and blue tiles will remain alongside the untouched yellow bow tie in the center.
Step 5: Pull the yellow blocks to clear the center bow tie shape.
As your light blue blocks and pink blocks finish their work, more waiting slots will open up at the bottom of the screen. The yellow bow tie is now fully exposed because the blue tiles surrounding it are gone. Tap the three yellow blocks from the bottom of your tray. These blocks have low numbers of 8, 9, and 8. Yellow ants will pour out of the nest and march straight into the center of the board. They will eat the yellow tiles very quickly. You do not have to worry about a jam here because the path is completely clear.
Step 6: Let the final ants clean up the remaining scattered tiles.
You have now pulled every single block from the tray. Your waiting slots will show the final countdowns for your remaining active colors. You might have a blue block down to a number 1 or a yellow block down to a number 2. The ants will run across the empty board to grab the very last pieces of the puzzle. Once the final tile disappears into the nest, the remaining ants will exit the board. The screen will clear and you will win the level.
Overall Strategy to Clear Level 2 Board
Control the flow of pink blocks at the very start of the match. Pulling all three pink blocks immediately gives your colony enough numbers to chew entirely through the bottom point of the heart. This creates two separate travel paths up the left and right sides of the board. Opening the sides early prevents a massive bottleneck. It lets your pink ants reach the top section without getting stuck behind the middle blue tiles.
Manage your full waiting slots with extreme care. When you pull the two light blue blocks in the second step, you completely fill all five slots. You must ensure that both pink and blue ants have active food targets. Because the pink ants can go up the sides and the blue ants can eat the middle, neither color gets blocked. This dual pathing keeps the numbers ticking down safely and prevents an instant game over.
Never pull blocks if their matching tiles are buried under other colors. The yellow bow tie tiles are completely surrounded by light blue tiles at the start of the level. If you pull a yellow block too early, those yellow ants will have nowhere to go. The yellow block will sit in your waiting slot and waste valuable space. Always wait until a color is exposed to the open board before pulling the matching block from the tray.
Pace your final tray pulls to keep the board moving smoothly. It is highly tempting to drag everything into the waiting slots as soon as a single space opens up. I strongly recommend letting the massive 37 and 38 blocks drain down to single digits before you flood the queue with the yellow blocks. Letting the big blocks clear out gives you plenty of empty slots for the final cleanup phase of the puzzle.
Final Thought
Clearing this level requires a steady pace and good slot management. The massive numbered blocks take plenty of time to count down. As long as you open the side paths early, your ants will never get stuck on the board. Watch the video above this article if any step is hard to follow in text. Seeing the ants move along the paths will help you understand the perfect timing for your block pulls.

Welcome to Colony Flow Level 3. I am Liam Stone and I write puzzle game guides based on playing every single level myself. This level presents a colorful red berry picture surrounded entirely by a thick dark border. You need to manage your tray blocks perfectly so your ant colony never runs out of open paths to their food. Let us break down exactly how to solve this board and keep your waiting slots completely clear.
Colony Flow Level 3 Overview
What You Are Working With
The pixel art picture for this level looks like a large red apple or berry. It features a solid red body, a green leaf at the top right corner, and a tiny white light reflection near the center. A thick dark outline wraps completely around the outside edge of the fruit. This border is your biggest obstacle because it completely blocks access to the inside red and green tiles.
Down in your tray at the bottom of the screen you have a mix of colored blocks with numbers on them. You start with two dark blocks showing 26 and 28. Below those are several red blocks including a 10, an 11, an 18, and a massive 50. Further down the tray you will find a green 28 block, a white 5 block, a red 52 block, and a green 10 block. The nest hole sits right between the tray and the picture. The ants will stream out of this hole as soon as you pull a block into one of your five waiting slots.
Level 3 Objective
You clear this level by matching all the colored blocks from your tray to the colored pixels in the picture until the board is completely empty. The ants must eat every single tile to secure the win. You lose the level if you fill all five waiting slots with blocks and no ants can reach their matching colors. Your primary goal is to always open a clear path for the ants before you pull a new color from the tray.
Colony Flow Level 3 Step by Step Solution
Step 1: Clear the outside border by playing the two dark blocks first.
You must start by targeting the dark outline that surrounds the entire picture. Look at your tray and pull the dark 26 block and the dark 28 block up into your first two waiting slots. Do not touch any red or green blocks yet. As soon as the dark blocks hit the slots, a swarm of dark ants will pour out of the nest hole. They will travel up the screen and begin eating the dark pixels on the outer edge of the fruit. Because the dark pixels are on the very outside, the ants have direct open paths to reach them without any other colors blocking their way. The numbers on your dark blocks will rapidly count down from 26 and 28 as the ants consume the border. This keeps your slots moving and prevents a dead end.
Step 2: Pull your first red blocks to follow the dark ants into the fruit.
Once the dark ants eat away the bottom section of the border, they expose the red pixels underneath. This is your signal to start moving red blocks. Pull the red 10 block and the red 18 block into your open waiting slots. Red ants will immediately spawn from the nest hole and run straight to the freshly exposed red pixels at the bottom of the fruit. Your dark blocks will drop to single digits and then disappear completely as the last outline pixels vanish. By waiting for the dark ants to break the wall first, you ensure the red ants have an immediate path to their food. This keeps the red blocks counting down and keeps your five slots from jamming.
Step 3: Bring up the heavy red blocks to clear the main body.
With the dark border completely gone, the entire red center of the fruit is exposed and ready to be eaten. You now have plenty of open paths. Pull the large red 50 block and the red 11 block up into your waiting area. A massive wave of red ants will stream out of the nest hole and flood the board. They will spread out across the bottom and middle sections of the red berry. The numbers on these large blocks take longer to count down, so you want them active early. The red 50 block will slowly drop to the 40s and 30s as the ants do their heavy lifting. Because there is so much red exposed on the board, these blocks will never stall in your slots.
Step 4: Activate the first green block to target the top leaf.
As the red ants clear away the right side of the fruit body, they will open a clear path up to the green leaf. Watch the right edge of the picture carefully as the red tiles disappear. Once you see the path open on that side, grab the green 28 block from your tray and pull it into a waiting slot. Green ants will spawn and travel up the right side of the board to reach the leaf. If you pulled this green block too early, it would just sit in a slot and block other colors from being played. By timing it right, the green ants immediately start eating the leaf and the number 28 begins to drop.
Step 5: Deploy the white block for the center reflection pixels.
There are only a few white pixels forming a reflection near the top left center of the red fruit. You must wait until the red ants eat enough surrounding red pixels to completely expose this white section. Once the red ants clear a path directly to the white tiles, pull the white 5 block into a free slot. White ants will emerge from the hole and head straight for those specific pixels. It is very easy to forget about this small white block and accidentally bury it under red blocks in your tray. Make sure you pull it as soon as the path opens so it does not hold up your progress.
Step 6: Empty the bottom of your tray with the final red and green blocks.
You are now in the final phase of the level and the picture is shrinking quickly. Look at the bottom of your tray and pull the remaining red 52 block and the green 10 block into your available slots. The red ants will join the swarm attacking the remaining red body while the new green ants will finish off the top leaf. Keep a close eye on your five waiting slots during this busy phase. Always make sure a block is actively counting down before you pull another one. The large red 52 block will take up a slot for a while, so let the ants work through it without crowding the board.
Step 7: Let the ants finish the last few tiles on the board.
At this point your tray is completely empty and all your remaining blocks are sitting in the waiting area. The numbers will all be dropping into the single digits. You will see ones and twos on your red blocks, green blocks, and your white block. The last few ants will run up to grab the very final pixels of the leaf and the central fruit body. You do not need to do anything else here except watch the board clear. Once the final pixel is eaten, the blocks will disappear from the slots and you will beat the level.
Overall Strategy to Clear Level 3 Board
Work from the outside inward to break the dark outline. The most common way to lose this specific level is pulling the large red 50 block or the green 28 block before the dark border is broken. The red and green blocks will have nowhere to go and will permanently clog your waiting area. Always play the dark 26 and 28 blocks first to guarantee a path.
Match your tray pulls to the exact paths opening up on the board. When the bottom dark border breaks, only pull enough red blocks to feed ants into that specific opening. Wait for the right side to clear completely before you pull the green block to feed the top leaf.
Hold the white 5 block until the red center is fully exposed. The white reflection pixels are completely surrounded by red tiles from the very beginning. If you place the white block in a slot too early, it will sit there completely frozen. Wait until the red ants eat their way into the middle of the picture before pulling the white block.
Balance your large number blocks with your small number blocks. You have massive blocks like the red 50 and the red 52 sitting in the tray. Pull these large blocks alongside smaller ones like the red 10 or the green 10. This combination ensures that some blocks finish their count quickly and open up their slot for the next color.
Final Thought
Beating this board comes down to strict patience and paying attention to the outermost layers of the picture. If you control the urge to pull the massive red blocks immediately and focus on the dark outline first, you will breeze through this puzzle. If you find any of these tray moves hard to follow in text, I encourage you to watch the video above this article to see exactly how I route the ants to victory.

Colony Flow Level 4 brings a massive colorful mushroom house picture directly to your screen. You have to feed a huge colony of ants while managing several different colors at once to beat this puzzle. I will walk you through exactly how to keep your ants moving and avoid filling your waiting slots. You will learn the exact order to pull your blocks so your board never jams.
Colony Flow Level 4 Overview
What You Are Working With
The picture in this level is very detailed and packed with different colors. You have a massive mushroom house sitting on a patch of green grass against a light blue sky. The house features a bright yellow base and a huge red roof covered in large peach spots. Right in the middle of the base sits a dark brown door wrapped in a solid white outline. A tiny yellow chimney rests on the top right side of the red roof. Your tray is fully packed with colored blocks that match all these specific sections. The numbers on the red roof blocks and the blue sky blocks are particularly high. You have five waiting slots positioned just above your tray. If you pull a block and the ants cannot reach that specific color on the board the block simply sits in the slot. If all five slots fill up and your ants stop moving you lose the level instantly.
Level 4 Objective
You clear the level by feeding every single colored pixel on the board to your swarming ants. You win when the mushroom house and the sky vanish completely and the board is totally empty. Your main goal is to pull blocks in a careful order that always leaves an open walking path for the ants to travel.
Colony Flow Level 4 Step by Step Solution
Step 1: Pull the green block to clear the grass and open the bottom paths
The green grass completely blocks the bottom edge of the mushroom house and the sky. You start your level by selecting the green block with the number 24 from your bottom tray. The ants immediately stream out of their nest hole and rush to the left and right sides of the board. They eat away all the green pixels resting at the very bottom. This is a vital first move because it unlocks the entire bottom row of the picture. If you skip the grass and try to grab the red roof colors right away your ants will get stuck. The red blocks would just sit in your waiting slots and waste valuable space. Clearing the green gives your ants direct physical access to the blue sky and the yellow base of the house. You keep your waiting slots safe by letting the ants finish the green grass before you crowd the board with other colors.
Step 2: Target the light blue sky to clear the outer edges of the picture
Once the green grass disappears you have a completely open path to the light blue sky. The sky surrounds the entire mushroom house on the left side and the right side and across the top edge. Pull the light blue block from your tray to send your ants out to the perimeter. The sky makes up a massive portion of the picture so the numbers on these blue blocks are very high. Watching the ants clear the sky is extremely satisfying and forms a core part of your winning strategy. Removing this outer blue layer means the ants have a clear path to walk all the way up the sides of the board. This prevents them from crowding in the center. You must leave room for the ants to walk around the sides of the mushroom cap later on. The blue blocks empty out your tray quickly and keep the ants moving fast without clogging your five slots.
Step 3: Break down the white door outline and start the yellow walls
Now you need to turn your attention to the center bottom of the board. The house has a door with a white outline that you must remove to reach the brown wood underneath. Pull the white block to let the ants run straight up the middle and clear that specific outline. At the exact same time you can bring up a yellow block to start eating away the yellow walls of the mushroom house base. The yellow base sits right above where the grass used to be so the path is completely open for the ants to climb. Balancing the white block in the center and the yellow block on the sides keeps your ants busy and moving smoothly. Your five waiting slots remain completely safe because both the white and yellow colors have immediate open paths straight from the nest.
Step 4: Clear the dark brown door to hollow out the exact middle of the board
With the white outline completely gone the dark brown door is totally exposed to your ants. Pull the dark brown block from the tray into your active slots. Your ants will rush straight up the center path to eat the brown door pixels. Clearing the center is incredibly helpful because it provides a massive shortcut for your ants to reach the upper sections later. The yellow walls are still shrinking on the left and right sides while the brown door disappears directly in the middle. You are essentially hollowing out the entire bottom half of the picture. Always watch the numbers on your blocks drop as the ants take bites. Once the brown and yellow numbers hit zero those sections vanish completely. This massive empty space guarantees your ants will never get stuck trying to reach the roof.
Step 5: Release multiple red blocks to attack the massive mushroom roof
The red roof is the absolute largest single section of this entire puzzle. You will need several red blocks to clear it all out. Pull the first few red blocks into your waiting slots now. Because you cleared the sky on the outside and the base on the inside the ants have multiple angles of attack. They will swarm up the outside empty edges and rush straight up the middle shortcut to eat the red pixels. The numbers on these red blocks are quite large like 15 and 30. You have to be very careful here not to pull too many blocks at one single time. Let the ants chip away at the red before you fill your fifth waiting slot. You never want to dead end the board by pulling a block that has no open path. Leaving at least one slot completely empty is a great habit to build.
Step 6: Send up the peach blocks to clear the spots on the mushroom cap
As the red roof slowly shrinks you will expose the peach colored spots. These spots start out totally surrounded by red pixels at the beginning of the level. You could not touch them earlier because there was absolutely no path through the solid red wall. Now that the red is partially gone the ants can easily reach the peach spots. Pull the peach block from the tray and watch the ants clean up those bright circles. Getting these spots out of the way creates huge empty gaps right in the middle of the roof. This helps the ants navigate much faster to the remaining red pixels at the very top of the board. Keep a close eye on your board and only pull the peach block when you actually see a clear physical opening in the red barrier.
Step 7: Clean up the final red and yellow pixels to finish the level entirely
You are now in the final stretch of the level. Only a few scattered red pixels remain at the very top of the board along with a tiny piece of the yellow chimney. Bring up the last red block and the final yellow block from your tray. The board is mostly empty now so the ants travel incredibly fast from the nest to their final destinations. The numbers on these final blocks are very low so the work goes quickly. The remaining pixels disappear in seconds as the ants wrap up their job. Your waiting slots are completely clear and there is zero risk of a jam happening this late in the puzzle. The final pixel vanishes into thin air and the last ant crawls back down the hole to secure your victory.
Overall Strategy to Clear Level 4 Board

The ants stream out of the nest hole in the middle of the screen and run toward any food tile that matches the color of the blocks in your waiting slots. As the ants grab the food the numbers on your blocks count down. When a block reaches zero it vanishes from the waiting slot and frees up a space.
You lose the level if you fill all five waiting slots with blocks that have no open paths on the board. When that happens the ants stop moving and you reach a dead end. Step 1: Open the board by clearing the yellow sand and green leaves

The numbers on your dark brown block will count down steadily. You now have three slots filled and two slots empty. Do not pull any more blocks yet. Just let the ants eat the sand the leaves and the dark brown border to open up the middle of the picture.
Step 3: Bring up the white block to feed on the inner coconut meat
The dark brown outline eventually breaks enough to let ants inside the coconut. Pull a white block into your fourth waiting slot. The white tiles do double duty on this board. They make up the tasty white meat inside the cracked coconut and they also make up the fluffy clouds high in the sky. The ants will always path to the closest available food first. Step 4: Add the light brown block to break down the main shell
The white inner meat and the dark brown outline are shrinking fast. It is time to clear the main body of the coconut. Pull a light brown block up into the waiting area. You must wait until two of your current blocks reach zero. Let the light brown block and the dark brown block finish completely. Once you confirm you have two wide open slots you can safely tap the connected sky blue boxes. The ants will sprint past the remains of the coconut and start eating the massive blue sky.

Pull the next set of connected boxes to keep the ants moving upward into the sky. The board looks chaotic but the paths are actually very wide open now. The ants travel fast across the empty bottom half of the screen to reach the sky tiles at the top.
Step 7: Clean up the final scattered pieces of the picture
The board is now mostly empty white space with just a few fragments of blue sky and white clouds clinging to the top edges. Your waiting slots should be clearing out rapidly as the block numbers drop to zero. Pull the final sky blue blocks and the last white block from the tray. The final ant will grab the last blue pixel and carry it home to empty your final waiting slot.
Final Thought
Beating this level is all about patience and slot management. The connected boxes can easily ruin your run if you tap them without looking at your empty spaces first. Just let the ants do their job and only pull new colors when you have guaranteed paths open.
